COVERED.meaning: Rule is closed for ACS coverage: directly covered, indirectly covered, or no standalone ACS check is required. See Notes for the reason.

NOT_COVERED.meaning: Rule is not closed by ACS coverage. It is either not testable by ACS or is a coverage gap. See Notes for the reason.

rules.rule_text: MPAM Requesters label every request to the memory system with an *MPAM information bundle*, comprising: - Two items that together identify a single partition: - A number called the *Partition Identifier* (PARTID). - A Partition ID space, called the *PARTID space*. Each PARTID space defines a set of PARTIDs. Each PARTID references one partition. - A *Performance Monitoring Group* (PMG).
rules.notes: Direct: feat001 checks PARTID disable behavior.

rules.rule_text: Each MPAM MSC implements zero or more *MPAM resource controls*.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: MSC may implement zero or more resource controls. ACS checks controls only when discovered.

rules.rule_text: Each MPAM MSC implements zero or more *MPAM resource monitors*.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: MSC may implement zero or more monitors. ACS checks monitors only when discovered.
Direct: reg001 checks MPAM version EXT bit behavior.

rules.rule_text: MPAM for RME requires MPAM v1.1 or higher, and requires support for 4 PARTID spaces. See [The MPAM for RME system](#BABHGIGGA6).
rules.notes: Direct: reg004 checks MPAM-for-RME feature requirements.

rules.rule_text: MPAM MSCs and MPAM PEs that implement different versions of the MPAM architecture are permitted to coexist in a system.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: different MPAM architecture versions may coexist. ACS validates each discovered MSC against its advertised version.

rules.rule_text: The requirements for memory behavior, including observation, coherence, caching, order, atomicity, endianness, alignment, and memory types, specified in the *Arm^®^ Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile architecture*, always apply regardless of any MPAM configuration or any MPAM partitioning of memory system performance resources. This includes all of the following situations: - When an MSC receives MPAM information bundles from one or more requestors, and those information bundles might contain different values, for example different PARTID or PMG values. - For all MPAM MSC resource controls and configurations. - When MPAM information stored with data accessed from caches is the same as, or different from, MPAM information in requests that access that data.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: base memory behavior rules always apply. No separate SYS-MPAM ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: The following physical PARTID spaces are supported: - Non-secure PARTID space. - If Secure state is implemented, Secure PARTID space. - If RME is implemented, both of: - Realm PARTID space. - Root PARTID space.
rules.notes: Indirect: non-secure PARTID space is exercised by ACS. Secure, Realm, and Root spaces cannot be directly validated from Non-secure execution.

rules.rule_text: Each PARTID can exist once in each PARTID space.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot compare the same PARTID across Secure, Non-secure, Root, and Realm PARTID spaces.

rules.rule_text: The scope of a PARTID is bound by its PARTID space. If a PARTID is used in multiple PARTID spaces, then a reference to that PARTID in one PARTID space does not also reference that PARTID in the other PARTID spaces.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot access all PARTID spaces to prove each PARTID scope is space-local.

rules.rule_text: The *Default PARTID* number, in each PARTID space, is 0. The MPAM architecture permits SoC designers to make non-MPAM Requesters label every request to the memory system with the Default PARTID.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot validate Default PARTID 0 across all spaces or non-MPAM requester labeling.

rules.rule_text: The *Default PMG* number is 0. The MPAM architecture permits SoC designers to make non-MPAM Requesters label every request to the memory system with the Default PMG.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot observe non-MPAM requester labeling to prove Default PMG 0 is used.
Not testable: requester-generation mechanism is system-wide. ACS cannot prove every PE, SMMU, GIC, and non-PE requester path.

rules.rule_text: MPAM Non-PE Requesters must use a mechanism that generates all the following: - PARTID space, to encode onto **MPAM_NS** or **MPAM_SP**. - PARTID. - PMG.
rules.notes: Not testable: non-PE requester-generated PARTID space, PARTID, and PMG values are not directly observable by ACS.

rules.rule_text: For non-MPAM Requesters, either: - There must be a system-specific mechanism that adds MPAM information to requests. - The non-MPAM Requester sends the default PARTID and default PMG, and sets the PARTID space. See [PARTID spaces, Partition Identifiers (PARTIDs), and Performance Monitoring Groups (PMGs)](#partid_spaces_partids_pmgs).
rules.notes: Not testable: non-MPAM requester default/system-specific labeling is not directly controllable or observable by ACS.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM MSC terminating Completer does not propagate MPAM information further downstream.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: terminating completer has no downstream MPAM propagation to observe. No ACS runtime check is needed.

rules.rule_text: When routing a request from upstream to downstream, an MPAM MSC intermediate Completer-Requester component passes the MPAM information unaltered to the downstream Requester port.
rules.notes: Not testable: intermediate forwarding of MPAM information is fabric behavior. ACS cannot observe the downstream bundle directly.

rules.rule_text: A buffered request must retain its MPAM information if the information is needed for operating MSC monitors or controls.
rules.notes: Not testable: buffered-request MPAM retention is internal. ACS cannot force or inspect a buffered request path.

rules.rule_text: A cache is only required to store MPAM information if such information is required to operate its implemented controls or monitors. See [Cache behavior](#BEICHBAF).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: conditional cache-internal storage rule. ACS checks observable controls and monitors when present.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM MSC responds to the MPAM information that arrives as part of a request.
rules.notes: Indirect: cache partition tests exercise MSC response to request MPAM information.

rules.rule_text: MPAM MSC partitioning controls find partitioning settings by the resource partition in the MPAM information of the request, and use those settings to control the allocation of a controlled resource.
rules.notes: Indirect: partition tests exercise per-PARTID control lookup from request MPAM information.

rules.rule_text: For caches, a cache line, which has an address, is always associated with the MPAM information of the request that allocated the line, or with the MPAM information of the request that allocated the line into an inner cache that has now been evicted to the current cache.
rules.notes: Not testable: cache-line MPAM metadata is internal. ACS cannot inspect the PARTID associated with each line.

rules.rule_text: The inner cache PARTID must be preserved when the line is evicted to an outer cache.
rules.notes: Not testable: cache eviction metadata is internal. ACS cannot prove PARTID preservation from inner to outer cache.

rules.rule_text: A PE might have integrated MPAM MSCs. These are discovered and configured in the same way as other MPAM MSCs. See [Memory-mapped Registers](#BABEAIBJ).
rules.notes: Indirect: all MMR-based tests use the common MSC discovery/configuration path, including integrated PE MSCs if discovered.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM MSC must support the physical address spaces that correspond to the PARTID spaces that it supports.
rules.notes: Indirect: non-secure PA-space access is exercised by ACS; Secure, Realm, and Root PA spaces are not directly accessible.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM for RME system includes at least one four-space region, but is not required to include any two-space or non-MPAM regions. More than one of each region type is permitted.
rules.notes: Indirect: reg004/reg005 check visible MPAM-for-RME and four-space capability.

rules.rule_text: A four-space region contains at least all the following: - One MPAM PE Requester that implements both FEAT_RME and MPAM for RME. - One MPAM MSC that implements MPAM for RME. Also, the interconnects support and propagate the **MPAM_SP** signal: +-------------+------------------------+ | **MPAM_SP** | Meaning | +=============+========================+ | `0b00` | Secure PARTID space | +-------------+------------------------+ | `0b01` | Non-secure PARTID space| +-------------+------------------------+ | `0b10` | Root PARTID space | +-------------+------------------------+ | `0b11` | Realm PARTID space | +-------------+------------------------+
rules.notes: Indirect: reg004/reg005 cover visible PE/MSC capability; Non-secure traffic exercises Non-secure MPAM_SP propagation.

rules.rule_text: A two-space region contains MPAM-compliant components and interconnects that support and propagate the **MPAM_NS** signal: +-------------+-------------------------+ | **MPAM_NS** | Meaning | +=============+=========================+ | `0b0` | Secure PARTID space | +-------------+-------------------------+ | `0b1` | Non-secure PARTID space | +-------------+-------------------------+
rules.notes: Indirect: non-secure traffic exercises Non-secure MPAM_NS propagation; Secure-side propagation is not directly testable.

rules.rule_text: If no MPAM PE Requesters implement Secure state, then the **MPAM_SP** and/or **MPAM_NS** encodings for the Secure PARTID space are unused and are RESERVED.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot generate Secure traffic or check reserved Secure PARTID-space encodings.

rules.rule_text: If a two-space region blocks downstream propagation of Root and Realm PARTID spaces from an RME MPAM PE Requester, then at the boundary where the four-space region ends and the two-space region begins, **MPAM_SP** must be reduced to **MPAM_NS** by using a *bridge*.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot observe 4-to-2 bridge reduction from Root/Realm MPAM_SP to MPAM_NS.

rules.rule_text: If a two-space MPAM MSC is downstream from a four-space MPAM Requester and a 4 to 2 bridge is used, the bridging scheme to reduce **MPAM_SP** to **MPAM_NS** is permitted to be static or dynamic.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot observe whether a 4-to-2 bridge uses static or dynamic reduction.

rules.rule_text: If a four-space MPAM MSC is downstream from a two-space MPAM Requester, then at the boundary where the two-space region ends and the four-space region begins, **MPAM_NS** must be expanded to **MPAM_SP**, for example by using a fixed mapping as follows: +------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+ | Two-space **MPAM_NS** input | Four-space **MPAM_SP**\[1:0\] output | +====================================+======================================+ | `0b0`, Secure PARTID space | `0b00`, Secure PARTID space | +------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+ | `0b1`, Non-secure PARTID space | `0b01`, Non-secure PARTID space | +------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+ : A two-space to four-space region fixed expansion scheme {#tbl:BABIJIHJE5}
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot observe 2-to-4 bridge expansion from MPAM_NS to MPAM_SP.

rules.rule_text: The requirements for bridges are: - Bridging must not alter the physical address space of a request. - Bridging requests that use the Secure PARTID space must not be altered to use a different PARTID space. - Bridging requests that use the Non-secure PARTID space must not be altered to use a different PARTID space.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot prove bridge preservation of physical address space and PARTID space.

rules.rule_text: The choice of not monitoring some transactions is not available on true two-space components. Support for the ability to mark requests with the NO_MON flag would require modifying the two-space component.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: design statement for true two-space components. No separate ACS runtime check is needed.

rules.rule_text: The MAP4SPTO2SP register must only be accessible in the Root physical address space.
rules.notes: Not testable: mAP4SPTO2SP is Root PA-space only; Non-secure ACS cannot verify Root-only access.

rules.rule_text: The external mapping register must only be accessible in the Root physical address space.
rules.notes: Not testable: external mapping register is Root PA-space only; Non-secure ACS cannot verify Root-only access.
Not testable: ACS cannot observe fixed MPAM_SP to MPAM_NS bridge signal mapping.

rules.rule_text: Non-MPAM components do not have the ability to: - Make requests with non-zero MPAM information or to use MPAM information when completing requests. - Propagate MPAM information to downstream MSCs.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot identify or control all non-MPAM components to prove they do not propagate MPAM information.

rules.rule_text: Requesters attached to an SMMU for RME are only associated with the Secure, Non-secure, and Realm Security states, and therefore use three of the four PARTID spaces.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS does not control SMMU-attached requester traffic or observe its PARTID-space use.

rules.rule_text: Completers that have no support for the MPAM information accompanying requests must be interfaced to the system by dropping MPAM information from the requests.
rules.notes: Not testable: completer interface behavior. ACS cannot observe whether MPAM information was dropped before a non-MPAM completer.

rules.rule_text: Interconnects connect Requesters to Completers, and they must transport MPAM information from MPAM Requester to Completer.
rules.notes: Not testable: interconnect transport behavior. ACS cannot directly observe MPAM information on fabric links.

rules.rule_text: If a cache stores MPAM information for a cache line, it must associate the MPAM information of the request that allocated the cache line with the data stored in the cache line. This stored MPAM information is a property of the data.
rules.notes: Not testable: cache-line MPAM metadata is internal. ACS cannot inspect whether allocated lines store the request MPAM information.

rules.rule_text: If a cache does not propagate MPAM information, it must be the last MPAM MSC on the downstream path. For a cache that does propagate MPAM information when evicting a cache line, all of the following apply: - When a cache line that is not in a last-level cache is evicted to another cache, the evicting cache must produce the MPAM information that is associated with the cache line. - If the evicting cache does not store MPAM information associated with the evicted cache line, it must instead produce the MPAM information of the request that caused the eviction. - A system cache (last-level cache) either: - Produces the MPAM information of the request that caused the eviction in its request to a memory-channel controller. - Produces the stored MPAM information associated with the evicted line.
rules.notes: Not testable: cache eviction propagation behavior. ACS cannot observe MPAM metadata passed with evicted cache lines.

rules.rule_text: A cache may optionally implement cache-storage usage monitoring.
rules.notes: Direct: CSUMON tests check cache-storage usage monitoring when implemented.

rules.rule_text: For a monitored PARTID, the monitor gives the total cache storage used by the partitions in the monitor's PARTID space and matching filter criteria programmed for the monitor.
rules.notes: Direct: CSUMON PMG/PARTID filter tests check cache-storage accounting for matching criteria.

rules.rule_text: If a write access, or a write-back from a cache level, associated with a request from an MPAM Requester, updates an entry that is present in the cache, it is IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFIC whether the cache entry: - Stays associated with its stored MPAM information. - Is updated to be associated with the MPAM information of that write access.
rules.notes: Not testable: write-hit cache-line association is implementation-specific and cache-internal; ACS cannot observe the chosen association.

rules.rule_text: A write hit to cached data is permitted but not required to change the portion of the cache capacity allocated to the data, if the resource partition of the cache data is updated due to the write hit, and the portion of capacity where the data currently resides is not in the new resource partition's cache portion bitmap.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: write-hit portion update is permitted but not required, so there is no mandatory ACS behavior to check.

rules.rule_text: After a system reset, only the resource control settings for the default PARTID in an MPAM MSC must be reset.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: reset/default-state behavior. SYS-MPAM ACS does not need a runtime check unless MPAM controls are discovered after boot.

rules.rule_text: Capacity-based partitioning of a shared resource requires measuring the usage of that resource by different partitions.
rules.notes: Direct: cache partitioning tests use CSU measurement to validate capacity-based partitioning behavior.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM MSC can contain one or more resource controls.
rules.notes: Direct: RIS tests exercise resource/control discovery and RIS-based control or monitor selection.

rules.rule_text: Although different resources can have different controls, all resource controls have the following in common: - Each resource control uses the PARTID and **MPAM_NS** or **MPAM_SP** signal from the incoming request to select the appropriate control parameters for the PARTID space. - The selected parameters control the MPAM MSC behavior, either to partition the resources or to control monitoring of resource usage.
rules.notes: Direct: partitioning and RIS tests exercise common resource-control selection using PARTID and RIS.

rules.rule_text: When RIS is implemented, an MPAM MSC must implement independent resource controls and two or more resources of the same type.
rules.notes: Direct: RIS tests exercise resource-instance selection and RIS-based control/monitor behavior.

rules.rule_text: RIS values are IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED. All resources in an MPAM MSC must have different RIS values.
rules.notes: Indirect: RIS tests rely on discovered RIS values, but uniqueness is not the primary assertion.

rules.rule_text: Any RIS value from 0 to [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).RIS_MAX can be assigned to a partitioned or monitored resource. There is no requirement that every RIS value be assigned to a partitioned or monitored resource.
rules.notes: Indirect: RIS tests use RIS values in the 0..RIS_MAX range, but sparse assignment is not the primary assertion.

rules.rule_text: If a partitioning control applies to all resource instances in an MPAM MSC, then this common control must be associated with [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS set to 0.
rules.notes: Gap: common controls can only be inferred when advertised at RIS 0. If identical controls appear for all RIS values, ACS cannot prove whether they are common or per-resource.

rules.rule_text: If there is only a single resource instance in an MPAM MSC, all partitioning controls must be associated with [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS set to 0.
rules.notes: Indirect: error009 exercises RIS no-control behavior, which covers unsupported non-zero RIS paths for partition controls.

rules.rule_text: To select the monitors for a particular resource instance, the value of [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).RIS must be set to that particular instance.
rules.notes: Direct: monitor RIS tests use MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL.RIS to select resource-instance monitors.

rules.rule_text: If a monitor is not associated with any resource or with the MPAM MSC, then that monitor must be associated with [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS set to 0.
rules.notes: Indirect: monitor RIS tests exercise RIS selection and unsupported monitor RIS paths; unassociated-monitor RIS 0 is not separately asserted.

rules.rule_text: All of the following are permitted in an MPAM MSC implementation: - Fewer RIS bits can be implemented than the architecture defines, but at least enough bits to represent [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).RIS_MAX must be implemented. - RIS values that are within the range of 0 to [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).RIS_MAX can represent undefined resources. - When selecting a resource instance, use only the implemented bits to decode a RIS value.
rules.notes: Indirect: RIS tests use RIS_MAX and undefined RIS paths, but do not directly assert every permitted RIS decode rule.

rules.rule_text: If one or more of the following apply to the value of [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS or [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).RIS, then the selected resource is undefined: - The value is greater than [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).RIS_MAX. - The value does not correspond to a resource implemented in the MPAM MSC. - The value corresponds to an implemented resource, but the resource does not implement any control or monitor corresponding to the selected RIS.
rules.notes: Direct: RIS error tests validate undefined RIS, no-control, and no-monitor selected-resource cases.

rules.rule_text: If an MPAMF ID register is accessed when [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS is an undefined value, all of the following apply: - All HAS\_\* fields in that MPAMF ID register must read as 0. - No error interrupt is generated and no error is recorded in [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).
rules.notes: Direct: error012 checks ID register HAS fields read zero and no ESR error for undefined RIS.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM MSC only supports physical PARTIDs and does not support virtual PARTIDs. Any virtual PARTID generated by an MPAM Requester is resolved into a physical PARTID before it is communicated with the memory system request.
rules.notes: Not testable: virtual PARTID resolution happens before the MSC. ACS cannot observe the pre-resolution virtual PARTID path.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM MSC with RME must support four PARTID spaces and four PA spaces.
rules.notes: Direct: reg005 checks MSC four-space capability when MPAM for RME is supported.

rules.rule_text: In an MSC with RME, [MPAMF_BASE_ns]{#MPAMF_BASE_ns}, [MPAMF_BASE_s]{#MPAMF_BASE_s}, [MPAMF_BASE_rl]{#MPAMF_BASE_rl}, and [MPAMF_BASE_rt]{#MPAMF_BASE_rt} must all be defined in the MSC firmware data. See [MPAM feature page](#BCFFGEHJ).
rules.notes: Indirect: ACS gets and uses MPAMF_BASE_ns from ACPI/platform data; Secure, Realm, and Root base fields are not validated.

rules.rule_text: Support for the resource controls and monitors in one PA space are not required in another PA space.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: allows controls and monitors to differ by PA space. No standalone ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: If all of the following apply, then an MSC resource can be partitioned: - The MSC supports MPAM on the upstream interface. - The MSC has one or more MPAM resource controls for that resource.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: defines when a resource can be partitioned. Actual controls are checked only when implemented.

rules.rule_text: If an MSC supports the MPAM RIS feature, the MSC can have two or more partitionable resources selected by [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS. For more information, see [Resource instance selection](#CHDFFBDF).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: describes possible RIS support for multiple resources. No standalone ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: An MSC can implement one or more of the following OPTIONAL standard partitioning control interfaces for memory system resources: - [Cache portion partitioning](#BABFEFDD). - [Cache minimum capacity resource control](#BJJHPLAOI8). - [Cache associativity partitioning](#BEIJDJECA7). - [Cache maximum capacity partitioning](#BABDJJJC). - [Memory bandwidth portion partitioning](#BABGCGEF). - [Memory bandwidth minimum and maximum partitioning](#CHDEIHFE). - [Memory bandwidth proportional stride partitioning](#Memory_bandwidth_proportional_stride_partitioning). - [Priority partitioning](#BABGAJJG).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: lists optional standard partitioning interfaces. ACS checks only implemented interfaces.

rules.rule_text: The presence of each standard partitioning control interface is indicated by a bit in [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr) or in a resource specific memory-mapped ID register. See [Memory-mapped ID register description](#ext.MPAM.ID_registers).
rules.notes: Indirect: partitioning tests check IDR support bits before exercising each advertised control.

rules.rule_text: A portion has all of the following properties: - It is a uniquely identifiable part of a resource. - It has a fixed size or capacity. - All portions of a resource are the same size. - A particular resource has a constant number of portions. - Every partition that is given access to a portion *n* shares access to portion *n*.
rules.notes: Indirect: CPOR and MBWPBM tests use portion/PBM width and allocation behavior, but do not directly assert every generic portion property.

rules.rule_text: The enabled status of a PARTID within a PARTID space is global to the MSC, and applies to all the other partitioning controls in that MSC. This functionality allows resources used by a PARTID to be rapidly reclaimed if software using the PARTID is exited or a system-wide mode change occurs.
rules.notes: Indirect: feat001 exercises PARTID enable/disable behavior; the global-to-MSC scope is not directly asserted.

rules.rule_text: A disabled PARTID behaves as if it is programmed to allocate no resource or allocate resource with the lowest priority.
rules.notes: Indirect: feat001 exercises disabled PARTID behavior, but this broader rule is not directly mapped.

rules.rule_text: When a PARTID is disabled by writing to [MPAMCFG_EN_FLAGS](#ext.mpamcfg_en_flags), hardware is required to preserve the PARTID settings so that those settings are used when that PARTID is re-enabled.
rules.notes: Not testable: ACS cannot directly observe preserved hardware settings across PARTID disable/re-enable; behavior can only give indirect confidence.

rules.rule_text: If RIS is enabled in the MSC, enabling and disabling a PARTID affects all resource instances in that PARTID. See [Resource instance selection](#CHDFFBDF).
rules.notes: Gap: needs a direct test to disable and re-enable one PARTID, then verify the effect across all RIS values.

rules.rule_text: The enabled status of a PARTID controls the behavior of the request PARTID, even when [PARTID narrowing](#BABHGJFF) is implemented.
rules.notes: Gap: needs a direct PARTID narrowing test that disables a request PARTID and verifies the enabled status controls request behavior.

rules.rule_text: The behavior of an enabled resource control is the normal behavior of that control using the programmed control settings.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: defines normal enabled-control behavior. Feature-specific tests cover the implemented controls.

rules.rule_text: The behavior of a disabled resource control depends on the type of control, as follows: - A fractional control behaves the same as if the control were set to zero. - A portion-based partitioning control behaves as if the control were set to allocate no portions. - In a cache, a disabled PARTID has the second lowest allocation priority. That priority is higher than the allocation priority of an empty cache line, indicating it is likely to be replaced. - When PARTID narrowing is implemented, the resource control settings could be shared by multiple request PARTIDs. Therefore, disabling a PARTID cannot make the resource control for a shared internal PARTID act as if it has no resource. Instead the disabled PARTID must act as if the request PARTID is temporarily mapped to an internal PARTID that has no resources assigned. This means that [MPAMCFG_DIS](#ext.mpamcfg_dis).NFU must not be implemented in an MSC that has PARTID narrowing. See also [PARTID narrowing](#BABHGJFF).
rules.notes: Direct: reg006 checks NFU is not implemented when PARTID narrowing is supported.

rules.rule_text: For resource controls, only the control for PARTID 0 must be reset, and that PARTID must be reset to *enabled*. Firmware must initialize all PARTIDs in all PARTID spaces to be enabled at system boot before transferring to software that might not support this capability.
rules.notes: Not testable: boot/reset enable state across all PARTIDs and spaces is not directly testable after firmware handoff.

rules.rule_text: Caches can be partitioned into portions, and those portions can be allocated to partitions.
rules.notes: Direct: partition001 checks cache portion partitioning.

rules.rule_text: When a cache request requires allocation of a cache line, the PARTID of that request determines which portions of the cache can allocate that line.
rules.notes: Indirect: partition001 exercises PARTID-based cache portion allocation.

rules.rule_text: Cache portion partitioning uses the generic portion control interface described in [Portion resource controls](#BEIBHIFG).
rules.notes: Indirect: partition001 programs CPOR through the generic portion-control model.

rules.rule_text: Each bit of a *cache portion bitmap* (CPBM) controls whether a partition is permitted to allocate lines in a particular cache portion, as follows: - If the bit is 0, then the partition cannot allocate lines in the corresponding cache portion. - If the bit is 1, then the partition can allocate lines in the corresponding cache portion.
rules.notes: Indirect: partition001 exercises CPBM permission bits through CPOR allocation behavior.

rules.rule_text: CPBM is an instance of the generic *portion bitmap* (PBM) described in [Portion resource controls](#BEIBHIFG).
rules.notes: Indirect: partition001 uses CPBM as the cache instance of the generic PBM model.

rules.rule_text: If a cache portion allocates a cache line as permitted by a CPBM, and the CPBM is changed such that the cache portion is not permitted to allocate cache lines, the partition ends up using more cache capacity than permitted by the new CPBM. If a previously allocated cache line is in a portion that is no longer allocable by the new CPBM, one of the following applies: - If that cache line is not accessed again, it will eventually be reallocated to a portion that is permitted by the CPBM to allocate cache lines. This represents a temporary misallocation of capacity. - If that cache line continues to be accessed, it can represent a long-term misallocation of capacity. The cache line allocated to the portion might be updated. See [Write hits may update the MPAM information of a cache line](#BABFFDJJ).
rules.notes: Not testable: cache-line portion after CPBM change is internal, and both reallocation and retained misallocation are allowed.

rules.rule_text: *Cache associativity partitioning* (CASSOC) sets the amount of associativity that the PARTID can use within any unit of associativity, as follows: - In a set associative cache, CASSOC sets the maximum fraction of the cache ways that a PARTID can allocate within any cache set. - In a fully associative cache, CASSOC sets the maximum fraction of all cache entries that the PARTID can allocate.
rules.notes: Direct: partition004 checks cache associativity partitioning.

rules.rule_text: Cache maximum capacity partitioning uses the generic maximum-usage control interface described in [Maximum usage resource controls](#BEICIBHJ).
rules.notes: Direct: partition002 checks cache maximum-capacity partitioning.

rules.rule_text: The [MPAMCFG_CMAX](#ext.mpamcfg_cmax).CMAX setting is a hard limit on the cache capacity. When a PARTID request requires allocation in the cache that is above the capacity set by [MPAMCFG_CMAX](#ext.mpamcfg_cmax).CMAX, that capacity cannot be increased even if there is unused capacity.
rules.notes: Indirect: partition005 compares CMAX with SOFTLIM disabled/enabled, but does not directly prove unused capacity cannot be used above CMAX.

rules.rule_text: If a cache line is unallocated or used by a disabled PARTID, then when [MPAMCFG_CMAX](#ext.mpamcfg_cmax).SOFTLIM is 1, the PARTID can allocate that line even when doing so exceeds the cache capacity permitted by [MPAMCFG_CMAX](#ext.mpamcfg_cmax).CMAX.
rules.notes: Direct: partition005 checks CMAX soft-limit behavior.
Direct: partition006 checks CMIN allocation-priority behavior.
Indirect: feat001, partition005, and partition006 exercise priority inputs, but not as a standalone priority table check.

rules.rule_text: When a PARTID makes a cache line allocation request, an allocation candidate is selected using the following steps: 1. All implemented MPAM cache partitioning controls are applied: - If [MPAMCFG_CPBM\ ](#ext.mpamcfg_cpbmn) is implemented, then only candidates that have the [MPAMCFG_CPBM\ ](#ext.mpamcfg_cpbmn) bit set are included. - If cache associativity partitioning is implemented and the request PARTID currently occupies at least the [MPAMCFG_CASSOC](#ext.mpamcfg_cassoc).CASSOC fraction of the associativity unit that the request addresses, then candidates are selected from lines currently occupied by the request PARTID. See [Cache associativity partitioning](#BEIJDJECA7). 2. The request PARTID allocation priority is compared to the PARTID allocation priority of the remaining candidates and those candidates that are occupied by a higher priority PARTID than the request PARTID are removed as candidates. See [@tbl:BEIHCDHDE7]. 3. If no replacement candidates remain, no line is allocated. 4. If there are remaining candidates with the same or lower priority than the request PARTID, then the implemented cache replacement algorithm is used to select between those remaining candidates.
rules.notes: Indirect: cache partition tests exercise allocation behavior, but do not directly assert each candidate-selection step.

rules.rule_text: The downstream bandwidth from an MSC can be divided into portions, and those portions can be allocated to partitions.
rules.notes: Direct: mem001 configures MBWPBM portions and validates bandwidth partition behavior with MBWU counters.

rules.rule_text: Each bit of a *bandwidth portion bitmap* (BWPBM) controls whether a partition is permitted to allocate bandwidth in a particular bandwidth portion, as follows: - If the bit is 0, then the partition is not permitted to allocate bandwidth within the corresponding bandwidth portion. - If the bit is 1, then the partition is permitted to allocate bandwidth within the corresponding bandwidth portion.
rules.notes: Direct: mem001 programs BWPBM bits through MBWPBM configuration and validates permitted bandwidth behavior.

rules.rule_text: BWPBM is an instance of the generic *portion bitmap* (PBM) described in [Portion resource controls](#BEIBHIFG).
rules.notes: Indirect: mem001 validates BWPBM behavior as a PBM-style bandwidth portion control.

rules.rule_text: An MSC can implement any of the following OPTIONAL methods of partitioning bandwidth use: - Minimum bandwidth limit available to the PARTID, even in the presence of bandwidth contention. - Maximum bandwidth limit available to the PARTID, either the strictly enforced HARDLIM, or SOFTLIM in the presence of contention. [MPAMF_MBW_IDR](#ext.mpamf_mbw_idr).MAXLIM reports whether a soft limit or a hard limit, or both, is implemented.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: lists optional bandwidth partitioning methods. ACS checks only methods that are implemented.
Indirect: mem002 and mem003 validate MBWMIN/MBWMAX fraction behavior, but not every bandwidth control type in the table.

rules.rule_text: Over the same data path, a concatenation of MSCs of any type listed in this specification guarantees an allocated bandwidth B_PATH where B_PATH is MIN(BW 0..N), and BW 0..N is the bandwidth BW allocated to a PARTID by one MSC.
rules.notes: Not testable: end-to-end bandwidth guarantee across concatenated MSCs is system-performance behavior that ACS cannot prove reliably.

rules.rule_text: The minimum bandwidth limit used by a request PARTID is regulated as follows: - If the bandwidth used by the request PARTID, as tracked during the accounting window, is less than the minimum bandwidth limit for that PARTID, then requests from that PARTID are preferentially selected to use downstream bandwidth. - If the bandwidth used by the request PARTID, as tracked during the accounting window, is greater than or equal to the minimum bandwidth limit for that PARTID, then one of the following applies: - If maximum bandwidth limit partitioning is implemented, then requests from that PARTID compete with other requests as described in [Maximum bandwidth limit partitioning](#CEGEFJCI). - If maximum bandwidth limit partitioning is not implemented, all request PARTIDs using bandwidth greater than the PARTID\'s minimum bandwidth limit compete for bandwidth and do not receive preferential priority. A request PARTID using less than the minimum bandwidth limit is more likely to be scheduled to use downstream bandwidth.
rules.notes: Direct: mem002 programs MBWMIN under contention and validates bandwidth behavior with MBWU counters.

rules.rule_text: The maximum bandwidth limit used by a request PARTID is regulated as follows: - If the bandwidth used by the request PARTID, as tracked during the accounting window, is less than the maximum bandwidth limit for that PARTID and, if implemented, greater than or equal to the minimum bandwidth limit, then all of the following apply: - If there are no competing minimum bandwidth limit requests, then the request is selected to use bandwidth. - All request PARTIDs using bandwidth less than the PARTID\'s maximum bandwidth limit compete for bandwidth. - If the bandwidth used by the request PARTID, as tracked during the accounting window, is greater than or equal to the maximum bandwidth limit for that PARTID, then one of the following applies: - If [MPAMCFG_MBW_MAX](#ext.mpamcfg_mbw_max).HARDLIM is 0, the request competes with all request PARTIDs using bandwidth greater than or equal to the PARTID\'s minimum bandwidth limit and less than the maximum bandwidth limit. - If [MPAMCFG_MBW_MAX](#ext.mpamcfg_mbw_max).HARDLIM is 1, the request is saved until the PARTID\'s bandwidth use drops below the maximum bandwidth limit. As the accounting window advances, the tracked bandwidth use resets to zero or otherwise decays, permitting the partition to again use bandwidth.
rules.notes: Direct: mem003 programs MBWMAX hard limits and validates bandwidth behavior with MBWU counters.

rules.rule_text: If both the minimum bandwidth limit and maximum bandwidth limit are implemented, [@tbl:CEGGDBCA] shows the request preferences. +-------------------+----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | If used bandwidth is | The preference is | Description | +===================+==============================================+===================+=========================================================================+ | Below the minimum | | High | Only high requests compete with this request[^a^](#fn.tbl:CEGGDBCA.a). | +-------------------+----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Above the minimum | Below the maximum limit. | Medium | High requests are serviced first, then this request compete with other | | | | | medium requests[^a^](#fn.tbl:CEGGDBCA.a). | | +----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | | Above the maximum limit, when HARDLIM is 0. | Low | Requests are not serviced if any high or medium requests are | | | | | available[^a^](#fn.tbl:CEGGDBCA.a). | | +----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | | Above the maximum limit, when HARDLIM is 1. | None | Requests are not serviced. | +-------------------+----------------------------------------------+-------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ : Preference of requests for bandwidth limits {#tbl:CEGGDBCA} [a.]{#fn.tbl:CEGGDBCA.a} Implementations might occasionally deviate from this preference order when servicing requests to meet other goals, such as avoiding bandwidth starvation.
rules.notes: Gap: needs a combined MBWMIN+MBWMAX test; current tests validate each control separately.

rules.rule_text: For PARTID requests, an accounting window tracks bandwidth use over a period of time. If one or both the minimum bandwidth limit and maximum bandwidth limit methods are implemented, they are applied to requests that occur during the accounting window.
rules.notes: Indirect: mem002 and mem003 validate MBWMIN/MBWMAX behavior that relies on accounting-window tracking.

rules.rule_text: Bandwidth that is not used by a partition during an accounting window does not accumulate.
rules.notes: Not testable: accounting-window carry-over is internal and implementation-dependent; ACS cannot reliably prove unused bandwidth does not accumulate.

rules.rule_text: If a fixed accounting window is used, then all of the following apply: - At the start of the window, the bandwidth history is cleared. - Bandwidth is tracked over the period of time defined by the window width. - Each partition is allocated bandwidth for requests according to the minimum and maximum limits set for that partition. See [Minimum bandwidth limit partitioning](#BABHHBAF). - When the accounting window width is reached, the bandwidth history is cleared and a new window begins. Any requests queued during the previous window can be serviced in the new window.
rules.notes: Not testable: fixed accounting-window state is internal; ACS cannot reliably prove history clear and new-window behavior.

rules.rule_text: Request priority or priority partitioning is used to resolve conflicting requests of the same preference. See [Priority partitioning](#BABGAJJG).
rules.notes: Gap: priority partitioning for same-preference conflicts is testable, but no current mapped test covers it.

rules.rule_text: If a moving accounting window is used, then all of the following apply: - Bandwidth history is never cleared. - Bandwidth history is tracked over the period of time defined by the accounting window width. - When a bandwidth request is processed, it is added to the accounting window. - When the age of a processed bandwidth request becomes older than the accounting window width, it is removed from the accounting window. A moving accounting window is relatively free of boundary effects.
rules.notes: Not testable: moving accounting-window history aging is internal; ACS cannot reliably prove request aging and removal behavior.

rules.rule_text: An implementation may use any other method for tracking bandwidth requests that broadly complies with the methods described above. For example, the tracked bandwidth might decay at a fixed rate proportional to the bandwidth allocation, but not below zero.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: allows implementation-defined bandwidth tracking methods. No standalone ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: Memory bandwidth proportional stride partition control is an instance of proportional resource allocation generic control.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: defines proportional stride as a generic proportional-control instance. No standalone ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: [MPAMF_MBW_IDR](#ext.mpamf_mbw_idr).HAS_PROP indicates the presence of a memory bandwidth proportional stride partitioning control interface in the MSC.
rules.notes: Gap: hAS_PROP advertisement is testable through MPAMF_MBW_IDR, but no current mapped test covers it.

rules.rule_text: An active implementation of memory bandwidth proportional stride partitioning is required to work with an active implementation of maximum bandwidth limit partitioning. When multiple bandwidth partitioning controls are implemented and active, it is possible that certain other pairs of bandwidth control cannot work together.
rules.notes: Gap: needs a combined proportional-stride + MBWMAX test; current tests cover MBWMAX only.

rules.rule_text: A PARTID can be assigned different priorities to different memory system components that implement priority partitioning control. For example, PE requests to system cache might have a higher priority than system cache requests to main memory.
rules.notes: Gap: different priorities per MSC are testable through priority controls, but no current mapped test covers them.

rules.rule_text: For a system in which the interconnect carries QoS values or priorities, these priorities arrive with incoming requests from upstream. When a system interconnect carries QoS values or priorities, requests arriving at an MSC have an upstream priority and all of the following apply: - In the absence of internal priority partitioning control, all of the following apply: - The upstream priority can be used by the MSC to prioritize internal operations. - The upstream priority must be used as the downstream priority. This is referred to as a *through priority*. - In the absence of downstream priority partitioning control, the upstream priority must be used as the downstream priority.
rules.notes: Not testable: upstream QoS priority arrival is fabric behavior. ACS cannot observe incoming interconnect priority signals.

rules.rule_text: Priority partitioning can override the upstream priority as follows: - An MSC can use internal priorities to control the internal operation of that MSC. - An MSC can set transport priorities for downstream requests generated when servicing an upstream request.
rules.notes: Not testable: priority override affects internal MSC operation and downstream transport priority; ACS cannot directly observe it.

rules.rule_text: Internal priority partitioning is OPTIONAL even if downstream priority partitioning is implemented.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: internal priority partitioning is optional even when downstream priority exists. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: Downstream priority partitioning is OPTIONAL even if internal priority partitioning is implemented.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: downstream priority partitioning is optional even when internal priority exists. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: The priority of a response through an MSC, from downstream to upstream, is always the downstream response priority. Priority partitioning never alters response priorities received from downstream.
rules.notes: Not testable: response priority is downstream-to-upstream fabric behavior. ACS cannot directly observe response priority preservation.

rules.rule_text: All of the following apply to MPAM v0.1, and from MPAM v1.1: - If [MPAMF_IMPL_IDR](#ext.mpamf_impl_idr) describes no IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED partitioning controls, then [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).NO_IMPL_PART must be 1. - If [MPAMF_IMPL_IDR](#ext.mpamf_impl_idr) describes no IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED monitors, then [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).NO_IMPL_MSMON must be 1.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: implementation-defined controls cannot be interpreted generically by ACS. No standalone ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: It is OPTIONAL whether an implementation supports mapping a *request PARTID* (reqPARTID) into a smaller *internal PARTID* (intPARTID).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: PARTID narrowing support is optional. ACS checks narrowing behavior only if implemented.

rules.rule_text: The reqPARTID to intPARTID mapping for a physical PARTID address space must be used internally and not for downstream requests.
rules.notes: Gap: PARTID narrowing coverage still needs dedicated work; no current test proves this behavior.

rules.rule_text: For each physical PARTID space, if [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).INTERNAL is 1, then the reqPARTID is mapped to the intPARTID in [MPAMCFG_INTPARTID](#ext.mpamcfg_intpartid).INTPARTID.
rules.notes: Gap: iNTPARTID mapping programming is testable when narrowing exists, but no current mapped test covers it.

rules.rule_text: The architecture defines the following MPAM resource monitors: - Memory bandwidth monitors. See [Memory bandwidth monitors](#CHDFEJBE). - Cache storage monitors. See [Cache storage monitors](#CHDFCJII).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: defines monitor types. ACS checks monitors only when the corresponding monitor type is implemented.

rules.rule_text: The PARTID used to filter a resource monitor is always a request PARTID, even if PARTID narrowing is implemented.
rules.notes: Indirect: PARTID-based monitor tests use request PARTID filters; narrowing-specific behavior is not directly proven.

rules.rule_text: Resource monitors are associated with a partitionable resource, but memory bandwidth monitors might be placed at the top level of an MSC. Monitors at the top level of an MSC are accessed with a RIS value of 0.
rules.notes: Gap: top-level monitor RIS 0 access is testable, but no current mapped monitor test covers it.

rules.rule_text: A memory bandwidth monitor counts downstream write or upstream read payload bytes that pass the monitoring point and meet the filter criteria.
rules.notes: Direct: MBWU tests count payload bytes during memory workloads using MBWU monitor filters.

rules.rule_text: If the optional capture register is implemented, then a capture event must be implemented. A capture event transfers a monitor count register to the corresponding capture register and optionally resets the count register. See [Capture event and capture register](#Capture_event_and_capture_register).
rules.notes: Gap: mBWU capture-event behavior is testable if capture registers exist, but no current mapped test covers it.

rules.rule_text: An overflow occurs when [MSMON_MBWU](#ext.msmon_mbwu).VALUE exceeds the maximum value.
rules.notes: Direct: MBWU overflow tests prefill the counter near maximum and verify overflow behavior.

rules.rule_text: [MSMON_MBWU_L](#ext.msmon_mbwu_l).VALUE is never scaled.
rules.notes: Gap: no current ACS test explicitly verifies that MBWU_L VALUE is unscaled.

rules.rule_text: An overflow occurs when [MSMON_MBWU_L](#ext.msmon_mbwu_l).VALUE exceeds the maximum representable value.
rules.notes: Direct: intr004 prefills MBWU_L near maximum and verifies long-counter overflow status/interrupt behavior.

rules.rule_text: If the optional capture register is implemented, then a capture event must be implemented. A capture event transfers a monitor cache storage usage register to the corresponding capture register and optionally resets the count register. See [Capture event and capture register](#Capture_event_and_capture_register).
rules.notes: Gap: no current ACS test triggers a CSU capture event; reg003 only rejects prohibited overflow-capture capability.

rules.rule_text: A monitor instance has a monitor register that contains a VALUE field and a NRDY field. For more information on the NRDY field, see [Not-ready bit](#CHDBFBGD).
rules.notes: Indirect: CSU and MBWU monitor tests read monitor VALUE only when NRDY is clear; no standalone structural check covers every monitor instance.

rules.rule_text: All of the following apply to the monitor register VALUE field: - When the monitor is enabled, the VALUE field can change at any time. - If the monitor counts events, then all of the following apply: - When a monitored event occurs that matches the filter criteria, the VALUE count increases. - The VALUE field can be reset so that the count is based entirely on the updated field. - If the monitor measures resource use, then all of the following apply: - The VALUE field measures bytes used in cache storage. - The VALUE field can increase and decrease as the the filter criteria causes resource use to change.
rules.notes: Indirect: MBWU tests verify VALUE advances/resumes and CSU tests read/write VALUE; no single test covers all VALUE-field behaviors.

rules.rule_text: If a write updates the VALUE field in a monitor register that counts events, then that monitor continues counting the monitored event from the new VALUE.
rules.notes: Direct: monitor008 writes MBWU VALUE to zero and verifies the counter resumes advancing after new traffic.

rules.rule_text: If a write updates the VALUE field in a monitor register that measures resource, then the VALUE field in that monitor is overwritten by automatic monitor updates.
rules.notes: Direct: overflow tests write MBWU VALUE near maximum and verify hardware traffic advances the counter.

rules.rule_text: A monitor register is permitted to be implemented as RO.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: monitor registers are permitted to be RO. No check is needed unless RW behavior is advertised.

rules.rule_text: If a monitor register is implemented as RW, it is not mandatory to disable that monitor to reprogram it.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: rW monitor reprogramming without disable is permitted. No mandatory ACS behavior to check.

rules.rule_text: For a monitor instance, when the events counted or the resources measured in the configuration and filter registers are modified, the monitor VALUE field continues counting or measuring using the new criteria without automatically resetting VALUE to 0.
rules.notes: Indirect: CSU monitor tests reprogram PMG/PARTID criteria on the same monitor and continue reading VALUE after new traffic.

rules.rule_text: If any monitor instance requires time to establish an accurate count or measurement when the monitor settings are updated, then the monitor instance NRDY bit must automatically be set to 1 when those settings are updated.
rules.notes: Not testable: nRDY=1 after settings update can be too transient to observe reliably in ACS execution.

rules.rule_text: For a monitor instance that measures resource, the monitor NRDY bit must automatically be set to 0 when the count or measurement is accurately represented in the monitor.
rules.notes: Direct: MBWU monitor tests fail if the monitor remains not-ready after update/wait paths.

rules.rule_text: For a monitor instance that counts events, automatic setting the monitor NRDY bit to 0 is not required. If automatic update is not implemented, the monitor instance NRDY bit remains set to 1 until it is set to 0 by software.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: automatic NRDY clear is not required for event monitors. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: If a monitor does not support automatic updates of NRDY, software can use that bit for any purpose.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: software-defined NRDY use is permitted when automatic update is absent. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: If the monitor instance settings are not updated again, the NRDY bit must automatically be set to 0 within the IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED time defined by MAX_NRDY_USEC. See [Performance-monitoring parameters](#BABBHBCF). MAX_NRDY_USEC is a discoverable firmware data value.
rules.notes: Direct: MBWU monitor tests wait MAX_NRDY_USEC and fail if NRDY remains set when the value is read.

rules.rule_text: When a capture event occurs, all of the following apply to the monitor instance NRDY bit: - The monitor register, including the NRDY bit, is copied to the capture register. - After the monitor register is copied, the NRDY bit is reset to 0.
rules.notes: Gap: needs a capture-event test that reads the capture register NRDY copy and verifies monitor NRDY resets to 0 after capture.

rules.rule_text: All of the following apply to capture events: - Capture events are available to all MSC monitors. - For all resource instances and monitor types, all monitor instances can be sensitive to any capture event. - For a PARTID space, every monitor instance monitoring that space must be sensitive to the same capture event. - For a capture event, every monitor that is configured to be sensitive to that event is copied into the capture register for that monitor.
rules.notes: Gap: needs capture-event tests across monitor instances and capture registers; current tests only check prohibited capture capability.

rules.rule_text: Capture events complete immediately without signaling that the event has completed.
rules.notes: Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies immediate capture completion.

rules.rule_text: An external capture event can be distributed system-wide so that all monitors sensitive to that external event are captured.
rules.notes: Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies external capture distribution.

rules.rule_text: A capture event is permitted, but not required, to reset the monitor after it is copied to the capture register.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: capture reset after copy is permitted but not required. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: When the monitor VALUE field exceeds the largest representable value, a monitor overflow occurs and sets the overflow status bit, MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL.OFLOW_STATUS, to 1.
rules.notes: Direct: MBWU overflow tests drive VALUE past max and verify OFLOW_STATUS or OFLOW_STATUS_L is set.

rules.rule_text: After the monitor overflow occurs, the monitor VALUE field wraps and might be zero or greater, depending on the counter increment or the measurement value.
rules.notes: Indirect: monitor007 verifies post-overflow counter freeze/advance behavior, but does not directly assert the wrapped VALUE.

rules.rule_text: Setting MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL.OFLOW_STATUS to 0 resets the overflow status.
rules.notes: Direct: monitor008 clears OFLOW_STATUS through MSMON_CFG_MBWU_CTL and fails if the status remains set.

rules.rule_text: The monitor configuration registers can be read and written regardless of the value of MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL.EN.
rules.notes: Direct: monitor tests disable the monitor, update MSMON_CFG control/value state, and verify the written state is usable.

rules.rule_text: For a monitor instance, all of the following optional overflow behaviors can be configured: - Signal an overflow interrupt. See [Control of monitor overflow behavior](#CHDDEEJBD0) and [MPAM overflow interrupt](#CHDCBCCH). - Freeze a monitor instance. See [Control of monitor overflow behavior](#CHDDEEJBD0). - If the capture register is implemented, then capture the monitor instance in the capture register. - Broadcast an external capture event to all MSC monitors. See [Control of monitor instance behavior on a capture event](#CHDEEEADE6) and [@tbl:CHDGGBJBE5].
rules.notes: Direct: monitor007 checks configurable monitor overflow behavior.

rules.rule_text: A group of monitor instances can be linked so that a capture event caused by the overflow of one monitor instance is broadcast to the other monitor instances, and those monitor instances respond to that broadcast capture event as an overflow. See [Control of overflow linkage](#CHDEIHHIG8).
rules.notes: Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies linked capture-on-overflow behavior.

rules.rule_text: Capture events are local to an MSC and are not broadcast to other MSCs.
rules.notes: Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies capture events stay local to one MSC.

rules.rule_text: When MSMON\_\ .VALUE is written, MSMON\_CFG\_\ \_CTL.OFLOW_STATUS is reset from 1 to 0.
rules.notes: Direct: monitor008 checks overflow status reset when monitor VALUE is written.

rules.rule_text: For an MSC, an external capture event is distributed to all monitors of all PARTID spaces.
rules.notes: Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies external capture distribution to all PARTID spaces.

rules.rule_text: A local capture event is distributed to monitor instances in all of the following address spaces: - If originating from the Non-secure address space, then the Non-secure PARTID space. - If originating from the Secure address space, then the Secure address space. - If originating from the Realm address space, then the Realm PARTID address space. - If originating from the Root address space, then the Root PARTID address space. - If originating from the Secure address space that has the [MSMON_CAPT_EVNT](#ext.msmon_capt_evnt).ALL bit set to 1, then both the Secure and Non-secure PARTID spaces. - If the capture event is raised by a monitor instance overflow with the corresponding MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL.OFLOW_LNKG set to 1 through 6, then monitor instances for the same PARTID space as the overflowing monitor instance.
rules.notes: Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies local capture distribution across address spaces.

rules.rule_text: For a monitor type that does not implement capture on overflow, if all of the following apply, then that monitor is permitted to signal an overflow linkage event to other monitor instances that implement capture events: - The monitor implements MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL.{OFLOW_INTR, OFLOW_LNKG}. - If the monitor implements the long monitor register, signaling an overflow linkage event of that register requires implementation of [MSMON_CFG_MBWU_CTL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mbwu_ctl).{OFLOW_INTR, OFLOW_INTR_L, OFLOW_LNKG}.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: overflow linkage event is permitted for monitor types without capture-on-overflow. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: For a monitor type that does not implement capture on overflow, if that monitor type implements MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL.{CAPT_EVNT, OFLOW_FRZ}, then a monitor instance that has not overflowed can be frozen by a capture event. This behavior requires that MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL.CAPT_EVNT is set to a non-zero capture event and MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL.OFLOW_FRZ is set to 1.
rules.notes: Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; current OFLOW_FRZ test does not verify freeze caused by a capture event.

rules.rule_text: Detected and undetected errors must not prevent the MSC from handling an MPAM request.
rules.notes: Indirect: error014 triggers a second MPAM error after the first and verifies ESR updates, showing continued MSC error handling.

rules.rule_text: [@tbl:BEIIIFFG] describes the errors recorded that can be recorded in [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE. All of the following apply to this table: - The selection of [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr) depends on the memory request Security state. - *MPAM error code* is the binary value recorded in [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE. - *Error name* is the error mnemonic. - *Error description* describes the reason the error occurred. - *Fields captured* lists the following other fields that are captured in [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr) when the error occurs: - RIS is the resource instance selector value captured in [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).RIS. This field is only available when [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).EXT and [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).HAS_RIS are 1. - PMG is the program monitoring group captured in [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).PMG. - PARTID is captured in [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).PARTID_MON on an error that captures the partition ID. Depending on the error, PARTID might be a PARTID_SEL field in a register, a reqPARTID, or an intPARTID. - MON_SEL is captured in [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).PARTID_MON on an error that captures the
