rules.notes: Indirect: error tests validate multiple MPAMF_ESR ERRCODE table entries and selected captured fields, but not every table row or security-state case.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM error always updates [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE, whether or not that field contains a previously recorded error syndrome.
rules.notes: Direct: error014 generates a second MPAM error before clearing ESR and verifies ERRCODE updates.

rules.rule_text: When a misconfigured RIS value causes an error, the [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).RIS field must be set to one of the following: - If the error is caused by MPAMCFG\_\* register accesses, then [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS. - If the error is caused by MSMON\_\* register accesses, then [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).RIS.
rules.notes: Direct: error013 checks MPAMF_ESR.RIS reports the selector RIS that caused the error.

rules.rule_text: If a write attempts to update [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).PARTID_SEL with an out-of-range value, then one of the following IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED behaviors are permitted: - [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).PARTID_SEL is updated without the implementation checking the new value. If the updated [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).PARTID_SEL is used to access a configuration register, an out-of-range PARTID error can occur ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0001`). For more information, see [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD). - The implementation checks the new value. If the out-of-range value is detected, all of the following apply: - [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel) is not updated. - An out-of-range PARTID error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0001`).
rules.notes: Direct: error001 checks out-of-range PARTID_SEL error behavior.

rules.rule_text: If [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).PARTID_SEL is out-of-range, then when writing any MPAMCFG\_\* register other than [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel), all of the following apply: - If the implementation detects the out-of-range value, an out-of-range PARTID error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0001`). For more information, see [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD). - Whether the implementation detects the out-of-range value or not, one of the following IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED behaviors apply: - The write updates the register using an UNKNOWN in-range PARTID. - The write is ignored (WI).
rules.notes: Direct: error003 checks MPAMCFG access behavior with out-of-range PARTID_SEL.

rules.rule_text: If RIS is supported and a write attempts to update [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS with an undefined value, then one of the following IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED behaviors are permitted: - [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS is updated without the implementation checking the new value. If the updated [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS is used to access a configuration register, an undefined RIS error can occur ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1000`). - The implementation checks the new value. If the undefined value is detected, all of the following apply: - [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel) is not updated. - An undefined RIS error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1000`).
rules.notes: Direct: error008 checks undefined RIS handling in MPAMCFG_PART_SEL.

rules.rule_text: If RIS is supported and [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS is undefined, then when reading any MPAMF\*IDR, or MPAMCFG\_\* register other than [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel), all of the following apply: - If the implementation detects the undefined value, then an undefined RIS error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1000`). For more information, see [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD). - Whether the implementation detects the undefined value or not, the value read from the register is UNKNOWN.
rules.notes: Direct: error012 reads MPAMF_IDR with undefined RIS, and error013 reads MPAMCFG after programming undefined RIS.

rules.rule_text: If RIS is supported and [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).RIS is undefined, then when writing any MPAMCFG\_\* register other than [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel), all of the following apply: - If the implementation detects the undefined value, an undefined RIS error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1000`). For more information, see [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD). - Whether the implementation detects the undefined value or not, one of the following IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED behaviors apply: - The write updates the register using an implemented resource instance. - The write is ignored (WI).
rules.notes: Direct: error008 checks undefined MPAMCFG_PART_SEL.RIS access and accepts ERRCODE 8 or RAZ/WI behavior.

rules.rule_text: If a read from an MPAM\*IDR or an MPAMCFG\_\* register detects an error other than one of the following, then that read returns an UNKNOWN value: - PARTID_SEL out-of-range error ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0001`). - Undefined RIS error ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1000`).
rules.notes: Not testable: read value is architecturally UNKNOWN for these error cases, so ACS cannot validate a required value.

rules.rule_text: For the partition selected by [MPAMCFG_PART_SEL](#ext.mpamcfg_part_sel).{RIS, PARTID_SEL}, if a write to an MPAM\*IDR or an MPAMCFG\_\* register detects an error other than one of the following, then the resulting control settings in that register are UNKNOWN: - PARTID_SEL out-of-range error ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0001`). - Undefined RIS error ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1000`).
rules.notes: Not testable: resulting control setting is architecturally UNKNOWN for these write-error cases, so ACS cannot validate a required value.

rules.rule_text: If a write attempts to update [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).MON_SEL with an out-of-range value, it is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED whether: - The value is not checked and all of the following apply to the out-of-range value: - The value is written to [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).MON_SEL. - When the value is later used to access an MSMON_CFG\_\*, MSMON\_\* monitor, or MSMON\_\* capture register, an out-of-range monitor selector error ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0101`) might occur. - The new value is checked and all of the following apply to the out-of-range value: - The value is not written to [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).MON_SEL. - An out-of-range monitor selector error ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0101`) occurs. For more information, see [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD).
rules.notes: Direct: error005 checks out-of-range monitor selector error behavior.

rules.rule_text: If [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).MON_SEL is an out-of-range monitor instance selector, then when reading any MSMON\_\* register other than [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel), all of the following apply: - If the implementation detects the out-of-range selector, then an out-of-range monitor selector error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0101`). - Whether the implementation detects the out-of-range selector or not, the value read from the register is UNKNOWN.
rules.notes: Not testable: read value is architecturally UNKNOWN for out-of-range MON_SEL, so ACS cannot validate a required value.

rules.rule_text: If [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).MON_SEL is out-of-range monitor instance selector, then when writing any MSMON\_\* register other than [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel), all of the following apply: - If the implementation detects the out-of-range selector, then an out-of-range monitor selector error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0101`). For more information, see [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD). - Whether the implementation detects the out-of-range value or not, one of the following IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED behaviors apply: - The write updates the register using an UNKNOWN in-range monitor instance selector. - The write is ignored (WI).
rules.notes: Not testable: post-write behavior is implementation-defined with UNKNOWN selector or WI, so ACS cannot validate one required result.

rules.rule_text: If RIS is supported and a write attempts to update [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).RIS with an undefined value, then one of the following IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED behaviors are permitted: - [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).RIS is updated without the implementation checking the new value. If the updated [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).RIS is used to access a monitor register, an undefined RIS monitor selector error can occur ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1010`). - The implementation checks the new value. If the undefined value is detected, all of the following apply: - [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel) is not updated. - An undefined RIS monitor selector error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1010`).
rules.notes: Direct: error010 checks undefined RIS handling in MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL.

rules.rule_text: If RIS is supported and [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).RIS is undefined, then when reading any MSMON\_\* register other than [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel), all of the following apply: - If the implementation detects the undefined value, then an undefined RIS monitor selector error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1010`). For more information, see [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD). - Whether the implementation detects the undefined value or not, the value read from the register is UNKNOWN.
rules.notes: Direct: error010 validates ERRCODE 10 for undefined MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL.RIS; read value is UNKNOWN and not directly assertable.

rules.rule_text: If RIS is supported and [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel).RIS is undefined, then when writing any MSMON\_\* register other than [MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL](#ext.msmon_cfg_mon_sel), all of the following apply: - If the implementation detects the undefined value, then an undefined RIS monitor selector error occurs ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b1010`). For more information, see [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD). - Whether the implementation detects the undefined value or not, one of the following IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED behaviors apply: - The write updates the register using an implemented resource instance. - The write is ignored (WI).
rules.notes: Gap: needs a test that programs undefined MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL.RIS, then writes another MSMON register and checks ERRCODE 10 or allowed write behavior.

rules.rule_text: If all of the following apply to an error condition, then an MPAM MSC implementation is required to detect and report that error: - At least one feature that can cause the error condition is supported. - The MSC is designed such that the error condition can occur. - Detection of the error condition is required. See [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD).
rules.notes: Indirect: implemented error tests exercise required reporting for selected supported error conditions.

rules.rule_text: If all of the following apply, [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr).HAS_ESR is permitted to be 0: - FEAT_MPAMv0p1, or from FEAT_MPAMv1p1, is implemented. - No error conditions meet the criteria in [PNPQQ](#PNPQQ).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: hAS_ESR may be zero when no reportable errors exist. No standalone ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: For the purposes of [QBQJG](#QBQJG) and [PFNBV](#PFNBV), below, all of the following are MPAM MSC selectors: - PARTIDs. - PMGs. - Monitor selectors. - In FEAT_MPAMv0p1 and from FEAT_MPAMv1p1, RIS values.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: defines selector types used by later error rules. No standalone ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: All of the following apply to the MPAM MSC implementation of a selector: - The implemented selector interface is permitted to be narrower than the full width specified by the architecture. - The MSC internal selector implementation is permitted to be smaller than the MSC selector interface. - Bits beyond the implemented width of any selector are permitted to be silently truncated without any requirement to detect or report bits that are non-zero at the time of truncation.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: selector truncation behavior is permitted. ACS only checks invalid selector reporting when required.

rules.rule_text: For a selector field width of n bits, if an MPAM MSC implementation supports a width smaller than 0 to 2^n^-1, then it is required that values within the field size that are not valid in the implementation be detected and reported. Detection can be applied after silently truncating to the supported bit-width.
rules.notes: Indirect: out-of-range selector tests indirectly exercise invalid selector detection.

rules.rule_text: If PARTID narrowing is supported, then the Unexpected INTERNAL error condition must be detected and reported ([MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is `0b0111`).
rules.notes: Direct: error007 checks Unexpected INTERNAL error reporting when PARTID narrowing is supported.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM MSC can generate the following interrupts: - MPAM error interrupt. The conditions that generate an MPAM error interrupt in an MSC are described in [MPAM MSC errors](#CIHHADCG). The responses of an MPAM MSC to an MPAM error interrupt are described in [Error interrupt](#BABEJFIH). - MPAM overflow interrupt. The conditions that generate an MPAM overflow interrupt and the responses of an MPAM MSC to that interrupt are described in [Overflow interrupt](#CHDCBCCH).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: lists possible MPAM interrupt sources. ACS checks only implemented interrupt behavior.

rules.rule_text: A four-space MSC is permitted to use either a Non-secure MPAM error interrupt or a Secure MPAM error interrupt for signaling an error associated with the Realm or Root PARTID spaces.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: four-space MSC choice of Secure or Non-secure error interrupt is permitted. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: If [MPAMF_ECR](#ext.mpamf_ecr).INTEN is 1 and any of the following apply to an MPAM MSC, an error interrupt cannot be signaled: - The MSC does not support any MPAM feature that causes that error. - The MSC is designed so that the error cannot occur. - The MSC is permitted to not detect that error. See [Required error condition detection](#BEIEEJDD).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: applies when no reportable error can occur or detection is optional. No standalone ACS check is required.

rules.rule_text: An MPAM MSC can implement the MPAM error interrupt as one of the following. - A level-sensitive interrupt. See [Level-sensitive interrupts](#Levelsensitive_interrupts). - An edge-triggered interrupt. See [Edge-triggered interrupts](#Edgetriggered_interrupts).
rules.notes: No ACS check required: error interrupt type may be level-sensitive or edge-triggered. ACS checks the implemented type.

rules.rule_text: When level-sensitive interrupts are implemented, the interrupt is active when [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is non-zero.
rules.notes: Direct: intr001 checks level-sensitive error interrupt behavior.

rules.rule_text: If an MPAM MSC implements level-sensitive interrupts, then that MSC cannot use an [MSI](#MDTerm.MSI) to signal an MPAM error interrupt.
rules.notes: Gap: level-sensitive error interrupt must not use MSI. This is testable if interrupt type is discoverable, but no current mapped test covers it.

rules.rule_text: When edge-triggered interrupts are implemented, the interrupt is generated when [MPAMF_ESR](#ext.mpamf_esr).ERRCODE is written due to an error.
rules.notes: Direct: intr002 checks edge-triggered error interrupt behavior.

rules.rule_text: If an MPAM error interrupt is signaled using an [MSI](#MDTerm.MSI), then an MPAM MSC must implement edge-triggered interrupts. For more information on [MSIs](#MDTerm.MSI), see [MSI error interrupt support and configuration](#MSI_error_interrupt_support_and_configuration).
rules.notes: Gap: mSI error interrupt requiring edge-triggered behavior is testable, but no current mapped test covers it.

rules.rule_text: MPAM MSC support of an MPAM overflow interrupt is OPTIONAL. If an MPAM MSC has monitors that can overflow, Arm recommends that the MPAM overflow interrupt be implemented.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: overflow interrupt support is optional. ACS checks overflow interrupts only if implemented.

rules.rule_text: For a monitor instance, if all of the following apply, then an overflow interrupt is generated: 1. The control register OFLOW_STATUS flag is 0. 2. The control register OFLOW_INTR flag is 1. 3. The monitor overflows, setting the control register OFLOW_STATUS flag to 1.
rules.notes: Direct: intr003 checks overflow interrupt generation conditions.

rules.rule_text: If an MPAM overflow interrupt is signaled using an [MSI](#MDTerm.MSI), then an MPAM MSC must implement edge-triggered interrupts.
rules.notes: Direct: intr005 checks MSI overflow interrupt edge-triggered requirement.

rules.rule_text: For all RIS values, the optional [MSMON_OFLOW_SR](#ext.msmon_oflow_sr) register summarizes the MSMON_CFG\_\ \_CTL monitor overflow status flags, OFLOW_STATUS and OFLOW_STATUS_L.
rules.notes: Gap: mSMON_OFLOW_SR summary behavior is testable if implemented, but no current mapped test covers it.

rules.rule_text: The MPAM MSC behavior is discovered and configured using *memory-mapped registers* (MMRs).
rules.notes: Indirect: all SYS-MPAM MMR-based tests discover and configure MSCs through memory-mapped registers.

rules.rule_text: MPAM MMR accesses of 32 bits are required to be single-copy atomic.
rules.notes: Not testable: 32-bit MMR single-copy atomicity is a bus atomicity property that ACS cannot prove reliably.

rules.rule_text: MPAM MMR accesses greater than 32 bits are not required to complete atomically.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: greater-than-32-bit MMR atomicity is not required. No ACS check is needed.

rules.rule_text: For each supported PARTID space, separate locks can be obtained to access the MPAM MSC resource controls in those spaces.
rules.notes: Not testable: locks are per PARTID space. Non-secure ACS cannot verify locks in Secure, Realm, or Root spaces.

rules.rule_text: The monitor configuration registers can have a separate lock or share the same lock as the partitioning configuration registers.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: monitor locks may be separate or shared with partition locks. Both designs are permitted.

rules.rule_text: For each supported PARTID space, separate locks can be obtained to access the MPAM MSC monitor configuration, monitor, and capture registers in those spaces.
rules.notes: Not testable: monitor locks are per PARTID space. Non-secure ACS cannot verify locks in Secure, Realm, or Root spaces.

rules.rule_text: IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED MPAM MMRs are permitted in the MPAM feature page at offset `0x3000` and greater.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: implementation-defined MMRs are permitted above offset 0x3000. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: All locations in the MPAM feature page at offsets less than the maximum MPAM feature page offset defined in [Permitted truncation of an MPAM feature page](#BCFEBHCG) are reserved. All of the following apply to locations within the reserved address range: - Reads and writes of unallocated locations are reserved accesses. - Reads and writes of unimplemented optional register locations are reserved accesses. - Reads and writes of locations that are greater than the implemented register width defined by the corresponding ID register, but within the range allocated by the architecture, are reserved accesses. - Reads of WO locations are reserved accesses. - Writes to RO locations are reserved accesses.
rules.notes: Indirect: SYS-MPAM tests access implemented MPAM feature-page registers, exercising the common register access path.

rules.rule_text: For each supported PA space, an MSC has an MPAM feature page defining the implemented registers used by that address space.
rules.notes: Indirect: non-secure feature page is exercised by all MMR-based tests; other PA-space feature pages are not accessible to ACS.
Indirect: non-secure feature-page base is used by ACS; Secure, Realm, and Root bases cannot be validated from Non-secure ACS.

rules.rule_text: The MPAM MSC feature pages in each supported PA space are not required to have the same base address. Arm recommends that the MPAM feature page base addresses in each supported PA space are sufficiently different so that the address ranges do not overlap.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: different feature-page base addresses are permitted and overlap avoidance is a recommendation. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: For a PA space, an MPAM MSC feature page is an address block with all of the following properties: - The base address must be aligned on a 4 KB boundary. - The feature page must be completely contained within a single 64 KB aligned memory block. - All MPAM MSC MMRs are contained within that feature page.
rules.notes: Gap: feature-page alignment and containment are testable from platform data, but no current mapped test covers them.

rules.rule_text: If the MSC implements non-MPAM MMRs and those MMRs are trapped to a hypervisor, then those MMRs are permitted within the feature page.
rules.notes: No ACS check required: non-MPAM MMR placement in the feature page is permitted only for trapped MMRs. No mandatory ACS check.

rules.rule_text: The Non-secure MPAM feature page must always exist.
rules.notes: Indirect: all SYS-MPAM MMR-based tests require the Non-secure MPAM feature page to exist.

rules.rule_text: If the MSC supports the Secure address space, the Secure MPAM feature page must exist.
rules.notes: Not testable: secure feature page existence cannot be verified from Non-secure ACS execution.

rules.rule_text: If FEAT_RME is implemented, then the Realm and Root MPAM feature pages must exist. See [Four-space MSC](#CHDIBBBBE9).
rules.notes: Not testable: realm and Root feature pages cannot be verified from Non-secure ACS execution.

rules.rule_text: If a read-only MPAM MMR has identical content across Security states, it is permitted to share that register across the corresponding feature pages. The following table lists the MPAM MMRs that are permitted to be shared between feature pages. +---------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+ | [MPAMF_IDR](#ext.mpamf_idr) | [MPAMF_IMPL_IDR](#ext.mpamf_impl_idr) | [MPAMF_CPOR_IDR](#ext.mpamf_cpor_idr) | +---------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+ | [MPAMF_CCAP_IDR](#ext.mpamf_ccap_idr) | [MPAMF_MBW_IDR](#ext.mpamf_mbw_idr) | [MPAMF_PRI_IDR](#ext.mpamf_pri_idr) | +---------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+ | [MPAMF_PARTID_NRW_IDR](#ext.mpamf_partid_nrw_idr) | [MPAMF_MSMON_IDR](#ext.mpamf_msmon_idr) | [MPAMF_CSUMON_IDR](#ext.mpamf_csumon_idr) | +---------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+ | [MPAMF_MBWUMON_IDR](#ext.mpamf_mbwumon_idr) | | | +---------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+ : MPAM MMRs that can be shared between feature pages {#tbl:MPAM.registershared.table}
rules.notes: No ACS check required: rO MMR sharing across security states is permitted when contents match. ACS cannot and need not check sharing.

rules.rule_text: A PBM is an MMR containing a vector of single-bit elements with all of the following properties: - The *PBM bit width* (PBM_WD) can be up to 2^15^ bits. - The PBM_WD is a multiple of 32 bits. - Element *n* is PBM\[*n*\] at the address (MPAMF_BASE + PBM_offset), where PBM_offset is the offset of the particular PBM register. To access the PBM\[*n*\], software accesses the appropriate 32-bit PBM register word at the address MPAMF_BASE `+ PBM_offset + ((n \>\> 3) & \~3)`, and then accesses the bit `(n & 31)`.
rules.notes: Indirect: PBM partitioning tests program CPBM/MBWPBM words using IDR widths and PBM offsets.

rules.rule_text: If the 32-bit word containing the highest byte of the PBM (MPAMF_BASE `+ PBM_offset + (PBM_WD\>\>3)`) has unused bits, those bits are RES0.
rules.notes: Gap: unused PBM bits being RES0 is testable, but no current mapped test covers it.

rules.rule_text: The effective fraction value is the programmed value plus one lsb. For example: 1) Software is using 16 fraction bits to target 50%. The closest hexadecimal value to 50% is 0x8000. Software offsets `0x8000` by one lsb and writes `0x7FFF`, and: 1) If the fractional control field is implemented as: - 16-bits, the programmed value is `0x7FFF`. The effective value is `0x8000`. - 12-bits, the programmed value is `0x7FF`. The effective value is `0x800`. - 8-bits, the programmed value is `0x7F`. The effective value is `0x80`.
rules.notes: Indirect: fractional partitioning helpers program values using percentage minus one lsb, and tests validate resulting behavior.

rules.rule_text: An effective fraction value of: - 100% is enforced by programming the fractional control field with all ones. - 0% is enforced by disabling the PARTID by writing the PARTID value to [MPAMCFG_DIS](#ext.mpamcfg_dis).PARTID. See [Disabling a PARTID](#MD_disabling_a_partid).
rules.notes: Direct: tests program 100 percent controls and disable PARTIDs through MPAMCFG_DIS.PARTID.
